meta.evidence_rule: Every column below is stated from the PRINTED HEADER extracted from the PDF's drawn text and correlated to the widget by rectangle geometry, never from the AcroForm leaf name. On both these forms the leaf names lie - see arguable A1-3 and defect D1.

how_to_read.contributed_by: Which form's printed table supplies this column. 'both' means both forms print a cell for the fact; '433a' or '433f' means only that one does and the union takes it anyway.
how_to_read.pdf_ceiling: The tightest /MaxLen across every printed slot that will ever receive this column. fill-433a.mjs HARD STOPS on overflow - it refuses to truncate a filed form - so the ceiling is a real input constraint, not advice. null = no /MaxLen on any receiving cell.
how_to_read.row_flag: A ROUTING DISCRIMINATOR: a column the engine reads off the row and the form draws NO CELL FOR. Keyed BY FORM — `{ "<form>": "<why>" }` — because the same column is a discriminator on one form and a printed checkbox on another, which is what made one key impossible. adapters/pdf/assert-row-shape-spec.mjs [A2] excuses the column from the reachability check on a form this names AND ASSERTS THE EXCUSAL: the column must be reachable on that form's accepting group neither as text nor as a checkbox. An excusal that excuses a bound column is a STOP.
how_to_read.printed_as_checkbox: A PRINTED CHECKBOX COLUMN: the form draws a checkbox cell for this column. Keyed BY FORM, and the value carries the evidence — the printed label's (page, baseline, x1) in the declared y convention, and the widget names the form draws. [A2] CHECKS these rather than excusing them: the column must be bound in the accepting group's `checkboxes` (not its `text`), unless `printed_but_unmapped_on` names the form, which is itself checked. This is the half of the old `row_flag` that was being excused from a check it would have passed.
how_to_read.printed_but_unmapped_on: The form PRINTS a cell for this column and the map does not bind it. A declared, reasoned gap — and checked, not trusted: naming a form that DOES bind the column is a stale declaration and a STOP.

arguable.claim: Two columns that look shared and are not.
arguable.case_against_merging: 433-A's vehicles.year is the vehicle MODEL year - it sits inside the printed column group 'Description (Year, Mileage, Make/Model, Tag Number, Vehicle Identification Number)', and 433-A prints purchase date in a separate 'Purchase/Lease Date (mmddyyyy)' cell. 433-F's other_assets.year is headed 'Year Purchased'. Same asset class, same four-character cell, same word, opposite facts. A union that merged them on the key would print 2020 - the model year of a Camry - into 433-F's Year Purchased column, or a purchase year into 433-A's model-year column, in both cases producing a plausible number on a filed collection statement with no error at all. Separately, 433-F's real-estate desc is headed 'Description/Location/County' and is one cell holding three facts, where 433-A splits description (36 chars) from location (unbounded, multiline). A value authored for 433-F would exceed 433-A's ceiling and hard-stop; a value authored for 433-A would print on 433-F missing its location and county.
arguable.resolution: Renamed apart to model_year / year_purchased in the vehicle class, not merged. Whether county becomes a real column is Principal's - see A1-7.

arguable.claim: Two backbone tables whose names both say 'credit card' and which point in opposite directions.
arguable.case_against_merging: Line 16 AVAILABLE CREDIT is credit the taxpayer HOLDS - limit, owed, available. Restated here because a spec that groups 'by asset class' invites exactly this merge, and because 433-F prints BOTH of them - Section D and Section E2 - using the SAME three AcroForm leaf names.

arguable.claim: One leaf-name triple on 433-F names THREE distinct fact triples depending on which subform it sits in.

arguable.case_against_ignoring: This is the same defect class already recorded for 433-A's vehicles table, where the leaf names Line18aMKMDL and p3_t22_18aMILE are swapped against the printed Make/Model and Mileage columns. Anyone extending 433-F's map to E1 or E2 by matching leaf names against the canonical row keys above will bind three columns wrongly, and the gate will pass - step 8 only checks that every field is in a state the map accounts for, never that it is the RIGHT field.

arguable.claim: 433-A's column header says 'Type of Digital Asset'; 433-F's says 'Type of Digital Currency'.
arguable.case_against_merging: 433-A's section heading enumerates 'virtual currency (cryptocurrency), non-fungible token (NFT), and smart contracts'. 433-F's says 'DIGITAL ASSETS (CRYPTOCURRENCY)' and its column asks for a currency type. A row recording 'NFT - CryptoPunk #123' is a correct 433-A answer that prints on 433-F under a header restricting the cell to a currency. Low impact, since the IRS reads both as the digital-asset schedule - but it is a label mismatch of exactly the A5 kind and is reported rather than smoothed over.

arguable.claim: Every valuation column on 433-A is dated; the same column on 433-F is not.
arguable.case_against_merging: 433-A prints an as-of mmddyyyy in the column HEADER of lines 13, 14, 15, 16 and 65, and the map binds each of those as a table-level scalar. 433-F prints no as-of cell at all, and its digital-asset column header says 'as of today', which on a signed form means the signature date. So one stored balance serves both forms, but on 433-F it is silently re-dated to the day the taxpayer signs. If the figure is three months old, that is a misstatement the form itself asserts.
arguable.resolution: The valuation columns are merged and the as-of stays a table-level scalar, because that is where both forms print it. The re-dating is Principal's to accept. A per-row as-of column would satisfy neither form - neither prints one.

arguable.claim: 433-F's 'Name of individual or business on account' may be the payment-processor fact.
arguable.case_against_merging: 433-F's E2 instruction covers 'credit card payments ... and/or digital assets wallet, exchange or digital currency exchange' - the same ground as 433-A line 62. But E2 prints ONE such cell for the whole section, not one per row, so it cannot receive a table. Binding a two-row 433-A table to a single cell would print row 1 and drop row 2, silently.

arguable.claim: No column supplies the property's county, and a nearby backbone fact looks like it does.
arguable.case_against_reusing: 433-F's real-estate header explicitly asks for County; 433-A's location header includes 'county' inside a free-text cell. irs433_county_of_residence exists on the backbone and is the TAXPAYER's county of residence, which for a rental duplex or a vacation property is a different county. Reusing it would put a confidently wrong county on a filed statement.
arguable.resolution: Listed in the real_property row as contributed_by 'neither-as-a-column'. Principal decides whether to create it. Cost if created: zero new HubSpot properties - it is a key inside an existing JSON array.

arguable.claim: A canonical column's ceiling is the MINIMUM across every printed slot that will ever receive it, and on 433-A that minimum is not even constant within one table.
arguable.evidence: real_property.description is /MaxLen 45 on slot 18a but 36 on 18b and 18c. business_property.description is 34 on 67a and 45 on 67b. payment_processor.name_and_address is 93 on 62a and 172 on 62b. A 40-character property description therefore fills 18a and HARD STOPS on 18b, because fill-433a.mjs refuses to truncate a filed form. The union makes this stricter, not looser: bank_account.account_number inherits 16 from 433-A line 65 even though line 13 allows 24, because one shape now feeds both tables.
arguable.resolution: The ceilings above are already the minimums. Reported because a reshape that adopts them will start rejecting inputs that pass today, and that is correct behaviour, not a regression.

cannot_reconcile.problem: 433-F prints ONE table - Section C, two rows - where the backbone keeps FOUR. Its only identity column is a single free-text desc, and its printed instruction requires that cell to carry make/model/year for a vehicle and the insurance company name for a policy.
cannot_reconcile.recommendation: Keep the four classes SEPARATE and have 433-F's map compose desc per class with a special.composite_* construct, the way it already composes the taxpayer's name and address. Do NOT introduce a stored description on these classes to satisfy 433-F - that would be a fifth copy of facts already held in make_model, model_year and company_name_and_address, with nothing reconciling them, which is the defect this whole exercise exists to end.
cannot_reconcile.residual: Two printed rows on 433-F for four asset classes. Any taxpayer with a car, a whole life policy and business inventory overflows Section C. fill-433f.mjs's overflow handling is 'log', so the excess is reported rather than silently dropped, but the printed form will be short and needs an attachment. That is a property of the IRS form, not of the schema.

cannot_reconcile.problem: 433-F's Section A is three printed sub-tables with FIXED two-row budgets each - bank 2, investments 2, digital assets 2 - not one pool of six. A canonical row shape cannot make a taxpayer's third checking account print, because there is no third row to print it in.

defects_found_while_specifying.what: Twelve mapped groups declared no `row_class`. check-row-shape.mjs skips every group that declares none - `if (!rc || !Array.isArray(rc.accepts)) continue;` - so nothing asserted that a row landing in those twelve printed tables was a row of that table's class. A row filed under the wrong group printed under a printed heading it does not belong under, on a statement signed under penalty of perjury, with every printed total still reconciling. That is defect D1 exactly, in the places the row_class construct was never extended to.
defects_found_while_specifying.the_set_was_derived_not_taken: D-05 was filed against 433-A's EIGHT. Enumerating every group on every mapped form gives TWELVE: 433-A 8 (household_members, digital_assets, life_insurance_policies, property_line_20, accounts_notes_receivable, business_property, payment_processors, credit_cards_accepted), 433-F 3 (digital_assets, accounts_receivable, credit_cards_accepted), 433-A(OIC) 1 (household_members). All twelve are fixed here. Fixing only the filed eight would have left the same defect standing on two other finished forms while the commit message said it was fixed.
defects_found_while_specifying.and_the_instrument_was_switched_off_by_a: The three on 433-F were invisible to assert-row-shape-spec.mjs [A3], which is the check written to find exactly this. This file declared 433-F's DIGITAL ASSETS, E1 and E2 tables "printed, not currently mapped"; claimsNothing() excuses that phrase from the routing assertion; and 433f.map.json has bound all three since they were authored, each group's own _why saying in terms that the shared row class binds. A stale claim in the spec turned off the assertion over three tables, and excusedClaims() printed all three on every run without anything comparing them to the map. Corrected above: ["digital_asset: A > DIGITAL ASSETS (CRYPTOCURRENCY) - printed, not currently mapped -> A > DIGITAL ASSETS (CRYPTOCURRENCY) - two printed rows, mapped at groups.digital_assets","receivable: E1. Accounts Receivable owed to you or your business - printed, not currently mapped -> E1. Accounts Receivable owed to you or your business - two printed rows, mapped at groups.accounts_receivable","credit_cards_accepted: E2 - printed, not currently mapped -> E2. Credit cards accepted by the business - three printed rows, mapped at groups.credit_cards_accepted"]
defects_found_while_specifying.how_each_class_was_settled: From the PRINTED PAGE. Every heading is located as drawn text by page-geometry.mjs, its coordinates quoted in the group's row_class._why, and its band membership asserted by verify-headings.mjs. No AcroForm leaf name was consulted: on this series the leaf names are what lied. Three pairs share printed vocabulary and are told apart by what the printed columns ask for, each argued in the group's _why: payment_processor against bank_account (both printed instructions name PayPal), payment_processor against digital_asset (both name virtual currency), and credit_cards_accepted against credit_line (both say credit card).
defects_found_while_specifying.personal_and_business_property_are_two_c: bank_account is ONE class split by an is_business_account discriminator; personal_property and business_property are TWO classes. That is not an inconsistency. The bank tables print the same four columns and the page itself carries the discriminating sentence ("Report Personal Accounts in Section 4."); 20a/20b and 67a/67b print DIFFERENT column sets - BUSINESS ASSETS prints a title-holder column and PERSONAL ASSETS prints none - so the spec already held them apart, and two classes is the stronger of the two guards: a business-asset row stored under PERSONAL ASSETS is a WRONG CLASS and stops the run, where a missing flag on one shared class would only be reported.
defects_found_while_specifying.no_row_moved: Proved, not asserted. Every group's heading routing was snapshotted cell by cell from the filled PDF before and after; verify-headings reports 0 findings on all three forms both sides. A row_class declares what a row must SAY it is; it moves no cell.
defects_found_while_specifying.status: RESOLVED. Twelve row_class declarations, eight unrouted blocks retired, three stale printed-table claims corrected.

V2-SSN.subject: Whether 433-F stores and binds the taxpayer's and spouse's SSN/ITIN
V2-SSN.ruling: Store it, and bind it on BOTH forms. Telephones bind too.
V2-SSN.reasoning_as_given: 433-A already maps AND stores it, so the recommendation to exclude it on 433-F would have left the same client pre-filled on one form and hand-typed on the other. The inconsistency was the defect, not the storage.
V2-SSN.status: IMPLEMENTED. 433f_tp_ssn and 433f_sp_ssn bind to irs433_tp_ssn_itin and irs433_sp_ssn_itin - the same shared facts 433-A uses, reused rather than recreated. All six telephone cells bind.
V2-SSN.scope_extension: The PII rule now covers INTERMEDIATES explicitly: fetched-record files, sample fixtures, logs and the HTML review page must never carry a real SSN, and no fixture may contain a well-formed one. The v2 fixture uses 000-00-0000, which SSA has never issued and never will - an all-zero area number is invalid by construction, so it cannot collide with a living person the way a plausible-looking test value can.

A3.subject: 433f_inc_pension and 433f_inc_ssa - pension and social security
A3.ruling: Keep the taxpayer/spouse split as the canonical facts and have 433-F's fill sum them. BUT if either component is absent, leave the cell BLANK rather than summing what is present.
A3.reasoning_as_given: A blank and a zero print identically, and a total built from half the inputs is a wrong number on a filed statement. Same principle as the allowable column, where a wrong figure is worse than a blank an examiner completes.
A3.status: RECORDED, NOT IMPLEMENTED. No fill was changed by the task that wrote this file.
A3.supersedes: crosswalk.433f.json arguable A3, which decided 'No - new facts irs433_income_pension_household and irs433_income_social_security_household'. Those two properties become unused under this ruling.
A3.implementation_note: The guard is 'both halves present, or blank' - never 'coalesce absent to zero'. It applies equally to the household_member count derivation offered and declined above.

A2.subject: 433f_exp_gas
A2.ruling: Stays bound to irs433_exp_vehicle_operating_costs, PROVISIONALLY. Escalated to the Owner as a tax-substance question, not settled here.

conflict_left_in_place.for_the_binding: 433-F's printed label enumerates the IRS Local Standards operating-costs definition verbatim: 'Gas / Insurance / Licenses / Parking / Maintenance etc.' Vehicle OWNERSHIP cost is carried elsewhere on 433-F, in the Section C Other Assets Monthly Payment column, so the cell is not a merged ownership-plus-operating figure.
conflict_left_in_place.against_the_binding: adapters/pdf/maps/433f.map.json's own special.notes asserts the opposite - that 433-F 'merges vehicle ownership+operating and parking/maintenance into gas_monthly'. The note predates the reset and was written when 433f_exp_gas had its own property, so the question could not arise then.
conflict_left_in_place.adjudication: The printed form is the better authority. The note is the map author's statement about the map, and the map is Principal's artifact. Both stay in place; neither is deleted, and the conflict is recorded here rather than resolved silently.

A2.status: RECORDED. Owner decides. If overturned: create irs433_exp_vehicle_ownership_and_operating and repoint one binding. No other row depends on it.

A2-3-v3.subject: The three tables still form-scoped on 433-F after v3: other_assets, real_estate, credit_cards.
A2-3-v3.ruling: other_assets stays form-scoped PERMANENTLY. real_estate and credit_cards are re-pointed at the backbone, after an ADD-only column migration on the 433-A side.
A2-3-v3.reasoning_as_given: other_assets is a content answer, not a naming one: 433-F prints ONE Section C table that receives four backbone classes (life_insurance_policy, vehicle, personal_property, business_property), so no single backbone property is its home. asset_class, not scoping, is what makes it safe. The other two had only their backbone counterparts' SHAPE against them, and shape is additive.

what_was_done.433a.map.json: groups.real_property gains union_columns [year_purchased, purchase_price, kind]; groups.available_credit gains union_columns [card_or_line_type, minimum_monthly_payment]. Both gain row_class asset_class, accepting real_property and credit_line respectively. ADD-ONLY: no existing column changed key or target, and none of the five new columns has a slot on 433-A, so none of them reaches a 433-A page.
what_was_done.crosswalk.433f.json: real_estate reclassified form_specific -> exact at irs433_real_property (backbone_key real_property); credit_cards -> exact at irs433_available_credit (backbone_key available_credit). meta.counts moved 2 from form_specific to exact.
what_was_done.portal: irs433f_real_estate and irs433f_credit_cards DELETED after confirming zero contacts held a value in either. The two backbone properties' descriptions were PATCHED to publish the canonical row — they had never carried a row-shape sentence at all, so the portal was telling the next form that eleven and five columns were the whole row.
what_was_done.proof: compare-filled.mjs, every AcroForm cell: 433-A 458/458 identical, 433-F 174/174 identical. Both forms then re-seeded and round-tripped through HubSpot on the new binding, also cell-identical.

A2-3-v3.what_is_still_form_scoped: Seven properties: other_assets (permanent, above), bank_accounts and investments (433-F's abbreviated slot vocabulary — institution / acct / type / balance plus a bp flag the backbone has no column for), and the four per-printed-row real-estate refinance scalars (433f_re1_year_refinanced and siblings), which asset-row-shapes.json declares ROW columns and which should be withdrawn in favour of irs433_real_property's shape when 433-F binds them.

A4-v4-the-spec-is-now-checked.the_finding: count-sweep [S-21] disposed of 269 claim sites in this file on the stated ground that its lists are 'asserted structurally by adapters/hubspot/validate-crosswalk.mjs, which fails when a declared column is missing from a claimed table', and [S-20f] said the same of the per-class column and printed-table lists. validate-crosswalk.mjs never opens this file. Nothing in this repo read it as data - check-row-shape.mjs names it once, in a comment. The largest blanket in the sweep stood over the artefact row_class routing is authored from, on a forward reference to a check that did not exist.
A4-v4-the-spec-is-now-checked.the_check: adapters/pdf/assert-row-shape-spec.mjs. A1 every accepted class is declared; A2 every contributed column is reachable on the accepting group, by its own key or by a declared and verified printed_as alias; A3 every printed table a class claims is either routed by a group or declared unrouted with a reason, and a stale unrouted declaration is a STOP.
A4-v4-the-spec-is-now-checked.what_it_found_on_its_first_run: 15 problems. One undeclared class (retirement_account, live on 433-A(OIC)); six unreachable columns, all on the 433-F Section C table, three needing a printed_as alias and three printed but unbound; and eight 433-A printed tables this spec claims that no 433-A group routes, because those eight groups declare no row_class.
A4-v4-the-spec-is-now-checked.what_was_fixed_here: The class was declared and the six columns were disposed. The eight unrouted tables are DECLARED and REPORTED on every run, not fixed - see D-05.

D-06.ruling: SPLIT THE KEY, AND KEY BOTH HALVES BY FORM.
D-06.what_changed: `row_flag` keeps the consuming code's meaning — a routing discriminator the form draws no cell for — and `printed_as_checkbox` carries the artefact's. Both are maps from form to evidence, because the printed page says the same column is one thing on 433-A and the other on 433-F.
D-06.what_the_printed_evidence_corrected: [D-06] reported the five columns splitting three load-bearing and two inert. That was measured on MAP REACHABILITY. Read off the printed page, all five are drawn as checkboxes somewhere: is_business_account and kind are printed on 433-F ("Check if / Business Account" over both accounts tables; "Primary Residence"/"Other" in each real-estate row) and simply not bound. So the split is not three-and-two by column; it is per (column, form), and three columns gained a declared `printed_but_unmapped_on: 433f` that nothing had ever said out loud.
D-06.what_it_widens: [A2] now CHECKS every printed_as_checkbox occurrence — it must be bound in the accepting group's `checkboxes` and not its `text` — and ASSERTS every row_flag excusal, which must be reachable on that form as neither. The old blanket excused five columns and checked none of them.
